title: Cone Invariance and Homoclinic Standing Waves for Cooperative Finite-Range DNLS Equations
abstract: We develop a constrained-power variational framework for positive homoclinic standing waves in one-dimensional discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equations with cooperative finite-range interactions. Starting from periodic lattices, we construct constrained energy maximizers and use the associated projected gradient flow to establish positive invariance of the cone of nonnegative, even, and unimodal profiles. A central result is that the monotone ordering of the interaction coefficients, \(a_1\ge a_2\ge\cdots\ge a_M\ge0\), with \(a_1>0\), provides the structural condition ensuring preservation of this cone under finite-range coupling. Under a strict maximum condition above the linear spectral edge, we obtain a uniform frequency gap and period-independent exponential localization. These estimates provide the compactness required for the infinite-period limit and yield positive, even, unimodal, and exponentially localized homoclinic standing waves as strong \(\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\)-limits of periodic constrained maximizers. Numerical computations for several interaction ranges and cooperative kernels illustrate the effects of extended coupling on dispersion and localization and support the periodic-to-homoclinic convergence predicted by the analysis.
summary: This work provides a rigorous mathematical framework to find localized, standing wave solutions (homoclinic waves) for discrete nonlinear Schrödinger equations with finite-range interactions. It establishes that the monotonic ordering of the coupling coefficients is the precise structural condition required to maintain the positivity and unimodality of the solution profile. The method successfully links variational energy maximization to the existence of exponentially localized states.
main_problem: The paper develops a variational framework to prove the existence and characterize the properties of positive homoclinic standing waves in discrete nonlinear Schrödinger (DNLS) equations with cooperative finite-range interactions.
main_result: The structural condition $a_1 \ge a_2 \ge \cdots \ge a_M \ge 0$ is necessary and sufficient for the projected gradient flow to preserve the unimodal cone, leading to exponentially localized homoclinic solutions.
method: The authors employ a constrained-power variational method, utilizing projected gradient flow dynamics and approximating the infinite lattice problem via periodic boundary conditions before taking the limit.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional DNLS lattice with a finite interaction range $M$, governed by a Hamiltonian derived from cooperative, finite-range coupling coefficients $a_m$.
key_observables: Homoclinic standing wave profiles, spectral gaps, exponential decay rates ($\mu$), and the invariance of the unimodal cone.
important_parameters: The interaction coefficients $a_m$, the power constraint $ho$, and the ratio of the nonlinear term to the linear spectral edge ($T_\infty(ho) > 2A$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of the unimodal cone $C$ and the strict maximum condition ($T_\infty(ho) > \Lambda$) to ensure compactness in the infinite-period limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral gap opening, the convergence of periodic maximizers to the homoclinic limit ($\ell_2$ deviation and frequency convergence), and the necessity of the ordering condition on the coupling coefficients.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the variational setting, proves cone invariance based on the kernel ordering, derives the localization criterion via the spectral gap, and finally confirms the existence of the homoclinic limit by passing from periodic to infinite-period constrained maximizers.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of localization and stability in nonlinear lattice models, particularly the identification of structural conditions (like kernel ordering) governing the existence of localized states, is highly relevant to understanding energy transport and defect dynamics in quantum systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Dispersion relations for cooperative interaction ranges M = 1, 2, 3 with normalized coefficients (8.1). All cases share the spectral edge Λ = 2, but the curvature at θ = 0, equal to A2, grows with M.

Figure 2 shows the corresponding constrained maximizers at ρ = 1, N = 181. In all cases the computed profiles are positive, even and unimodal, consistently with the invariant-cone construction: the smallest monotonicity defect in the core of the profile is positive, of order 10−6 or larger, for every kernel satisfying (A2). At fixed power and total coupling, increasing M broadens the state and reduces its peak amplitude.
